item.title: Galaxy Stadium contract details revealed for Texas Tech football
item.description: Texas Tech's 15-year contract with Galaxy Digital Holdings LP begins with Tech due to receive $4 million in sponsorship fees for 2026-27. With 3% annual increases, the payments top $5 million for 2034-35 and exceed $6 million for 2040-41, the final year. The sponsorship fees for each contract year are due in two equal installments, half on July 1 and the other half on Jan. 1. The annual fee payments add up to $74,395,650. The agreement gives the company naming rights on Galaxy Stadium, the Texas Tech football team's home field . More: WVU run game the challenge this week for Texas Tech football | Williams More: Texas Tech interest in new NIL collective on hold, Kirby Hocutt says Tech released the contract on Thursday, Nov. 5, after a ruling by the state attorney general's office. The Avalanche-Journal filed a public-records request for the contract on July 17 after Tech and Galaxy announced their new partnership. Tech deferred to the state attorney general's office for an open-records decision. Though Tech took no position as to whether the information should be exempted from disclosure, its filing allowed Galaxy time to make arguments if it believed its proprietary interests could be compromised. The AG's office issued a ruling on Oct. 2. "As of the date of this letter," assistant AG Campbell Garrett wrote, "we have not received comments from Galaxy explaining why the submitted information should not be released. Therefore, we have no basis to conclude Galaxy has a protected proprietary interest in the submitted information." An opt-out clause in the agreement gives Galaxy sole discretion to terminate the contract on June 30, 2036, by giving the university written notice by Jan. 1, 2035. Each side also may terminate if either breaches the agreement in any of multiple ways accounted for in the contract or if either is unable to provide the agreed-upon benefits. The contract gives Galaxy an exclusive negotiating period to renew as the agreement nears conclusion. After the negotiating window expires, Galaxy still has 30 days to match other offers and enter into a new naming rights agreement at the matching terms. The venue where the Red Raiders play home games was known as Jones Stadium beginning in November 1947, then Jones SBC Stadium from 2000-06 and Jones AT&T Stadium from 2006-2026. Even though it's unlikely to come into play, Galaxy has a contractual guarantee that Tech will host at least six home games a year against NCAA Division I opponents, which includes FBS and FCS programs. In the event Tech failed to schedule at least six home games against Division I teams, the contract says the two sides "will discuss a mutually agreeable resolution" to ensure Galaxy still gets the full value of its sponsorship fee for that year. FBS teams started playing a 12-game regular-season schedule in 2006, and Tech last played only five home games in 2004. item.title: FSU football eyes fresh start under Rick Stockstill
item.description: When Florida State football plays Boston College at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill on Saturday, things will look different. Most obviously, the Seminoles (3-5, 1-4 ACC) will be under the direction of a new head coach for the first time in seven seasons, with interim head coach Rick Stockstill wearing the headset once again. The program fired Mike Norvell on Sunday, Nov. 1, after a 36-24 loss to Clemson that featured a mostly empty Doak Campbell Stadium in the fourth quarter and a misspelled plane banner calling for Norvell's removal. The game was labeled as a "defining moment" for university president Richard McCullough, who ultimately relieved Norvell of his duties. It leaves Stockstill with four games to try and avoid a third consecutive losing season for the program, and it starts with the road trip to Boston College. If the Seminoles are going to win a first road game in nearly three years, it might be because of the "subtle" changes that Stockstill said he'd make to the program's game day operation. "There'll be some subtle changes, some little things different... You can't come in and do a lot of wholesale changes schematically, you know, in the ninth week or the 10th week of the season," Stockstill said. "So there will be some changes." Stockstill won't "overload" Ashton Daniels, Tim Harris Jr. calling plays One of the first things Stockstill has to navigate is the change in offensive play caller. While Tim Harris Jr. served as the program's offensive coordinator under Norvell, the former head coach called the plays. Harris is now the play caller, and while his offensive philosophy isn't dissimilar to Norvell's, there will be some alterations. Harris, in his time at UCF, Florida International, and as head coach at Booker. T. Washington had explosive offenses that leaned on the run game. It's similar to Norvell, but pre-snap motions and misdirection might play more of a factor in Harris's offense. With Ashon Daniels under center, the quarterback is a capable fit for Harris. He was initially brought in by Gus Malzahn before his retirement, and Harris's offense won't be far off what Malzahn ran. For Stockstill, the biggest thing he wants to take some stuff off Daniels plate. "He is a strong, powerful runner that can move the sticks for you. I think he does a lot of good things. And to me, we just got to, you know, don't overload him," Stockstill said. "To me, that's the worst thing you can do with a quarterback is put so much on his plate, so many checks that he forgets about something simple over here because he's thinking so much." How that shows up in play calling will be something to monitor. Daniels was used heavily in the run-pass-option (RPO) game under Norvell, and had varied results. Even if Harris continues to put him in those situations, expect a simplified approach to get the ball out of Daniels' hands quicker, or handed off to the runner. item.title: Why Texas Tech basketball's shooting struggles don't concern Grant McCasland
item.description: Watching Grant McCasland on the United Supermarkets Arena sidelines Thursday night , it would've been hard to tell the Texas Tech basketball team was in a slog. The 19th-ranked Red Raiders were having another poor offensive performance, and Bethune-Cookman took advantage, cutting Tech's lead down to six midway through the second half. McCasland was still coaching, no doubt. He got into the face of several players throughout the night, questioning the likes of Josiah Moseley and Dra Gibbs-Lawhorn for lapses on the defensive end. Before and after those moments, though, McCasland often sported an almost cocky smirk. His team shot just 42% on the night, 30% from 3-point range and missed 12 free throws. The 76-58 victory over the Wildcats wasn't close to the 34-point win over Jackson State in the season opener. In years past, this is where McCasland would be reacting to each miscue and missed shot with an angst and sense of urgency. Those problems aren't present with the Texas Tech head coach right now. He knows the team he has, even if it isn't fully present in the first week of November. "I do feel more confident in the work that we've put in in practices," McCasland said, "because I know what I've seen, and I will tell you, last year we probably had three practices that we had everybody out there the entire fall. ... Literally, we had like eight people practicing. It's just hard to get. ... and what we've done this year is we've gone us versus us, and I've seen us do things that I know we're capable of doing in the game." Dra Gibbs-Lawhorn sees the same as his coach. The UNLV transfer had his breakout performance for the Red Raiders, going for a game-high 25 points on 7-of-14 from the field. While the Red Raiders are only shooting 26.7% from distance in the first two games of the season, the process matters more than the early results. "Whenever we get fatigued or getting tired, the flow of the offense is just so unselfish," Gibbs-Lawhorn said, "and it's just amazing. It's amazing to be part of a team that moves the ball every day." One of the players who McCasland didn't have throughout last year's early practices was Josiah Moseley, who fractured his foot in the preseason and didn't take the floor until late January. He's made up for lost time this season, registering 12 points and nine rebounds against Bethune-Cookman a game after producing 13 points and eight boards against Jackson State. "I think it's a big difference between this year and last year," Moseley said. "I didn't get the same reps in practice or in the game, so definitely did make things a lot easier, better. I know what I'm doing now and just transitioning from practice to the games is a lot easier." Another aspect of McCasland's sunny disposition as of late is Texas Tech's defense, which forced another 18 turnovers and came up with nine steals on Thursday. item.title: Oregon was a CFP favorite. What went wrong before facing Ohio State?
item.description: Analysts and oddsmakers viewed Ohio State and Oregon football as two of the titans of the FBS entering the season and as favorites to win the national championship . But ahead of their matchup, both teams sit outside the College Football Playoff . The Buckeyes suffered their second loss of the season on Oct. 31, losing 30-18 to USC. True freshman quarterback Luke Fahey started in place of Julian Sayin, who is out with an unspecified injury. After the loss, the Buckeyes received a No. 12 ranking in the CFP top 25, the first team outside the projected bracket. Like the Buckeyes, Oregon is also without its original starting quarterback. The Ducks are 5-3, ranked No. 23 with an outside chance of making the 12-team playoff. Read below about Oregon's up-and-down season below. What went wrong with Oregon football this season? Oregon had the fourth-highest preseason odds of winning the national championship at +800, according to BetMGM. The Ducks returned starting quarterback Dante Moore, who was seen as a top-five pick in last year's NFL draft before committing to a final year at Oregon. Oregon also retained standout defensive linemen Bear Alexander and A'Mauri Washington and acquired veteran Minnesota safety Koi Perich and UNC defensive tackle D'Antre Robinson in the transfer portal. Despite all the established talent, in Week 2, Oregon lost to unranked Oklahoma State, 39-31 while allowing 554 yards of offense. After beating Portland State 84-0 in Week 3, the Ducks faced USC at home. During the second quarter, Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens hit Moore while he was sliding toward the first-down marker on a scramble. Moore immediately exhibited symptoms of head trauma and was stretchered off the field. Stephens, meanwhile, was ejected from the game for an illegal hit. item.title: 'Hard yards' and a Prague summit
item.description: [Getty Images] For many Bournemouth followers, "doing the hard yards" meant following the team in their League Two days, spending every other Saturday heading to cold northern outposts such as Bury or Rochdale, or further still, Carlisle or Hartlepool. On Thursday evening, hundreds of Cherries fans who had made the journey to Prague and had gathered in the Old Town Square, embarked on the traditional European "fan walk" to the stadium. Having crossed the river still in good spirits, the steep walk up more than a dozen flights of steps into Letna Park dampened that enthusiasm slightly, with some comparing it to the gargantuan climb up into the gods to reach the away end at Newcastle United's St James' Park. The "hard yards" were not yet over, as with Sparta Prague's Epet Arena in sight, supporters were held up by police, and then seemingly directed away from the stadium and down residential streets before finally reaching the away fans' section on the far side of the ground, with kick-off fast approaching. It did not look like it would be Bournemouth's night after Lewis Cook missed a penalty and Sparta took a 1-0 half-time lead to end the Cherries' run of six clean sheets. Cook is not known for his goalscoring prowess, with a record of four goals in 318 appearances across his 10-year Bournemouth career. In his defence, the Cherries' two regular penalty-takers, Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier, were on the substitutes' bench at the time, while Cook did have a perfect three-from-three record in penalty shootouts, netting against Norwich in 2022, Wolves in 2025 and Newcastle earlier this year. Despite having made eight changes for the Sparta game, boss Marco Rose was not to be denied, and was again vindicated in his choice of substitutions as Tyler Adams, Evanilson and Rayan all came off the bench to score in a 3-1 win. So, those who had done the "hard yards" were rewarded with a seventh successive win in all competitions and a continued 100% record in the Europa League. Although some, understandably, took a more leisurely tram ride back to the city centre. Explore Bournemouth content on BBC Sounds

item.description: PICKERINGTON — When the boys cross country team is competing for and earning state championship and runner-up trophies, the Mount Gilead girls team can get overlooked. The boys have won a pair of state championships and three second-place finishes since 2019, but the girls have been active on the state scene, too. The program was state runners-up in 2017 and has gone to state as a group 13 times since 2009. There was a bit of a drop off with just one appearance since 2021, last going in 2024, but the girls find themselves back at the state meet as a team for 2026. "One of the downsides of our poor girls is that sometimes I think they look at the boys team and think they're not as good," MG coach Jake Hayes said. "That's been a battle, especially with them being so young." Mount Gilead got a surge of confidence during the regional run at Pickerington North Oct. 31 when it finished third to easily advance to the Division IV girls state meet at 3:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, at Fortress Obetz. "Getting to a regional meet is not something everybody does. Just because we do it a lot doesn't mean it happens all the time," he said. "Getting to a state tournament is a big deal. They were seeded fourth today (at the regional). Mechanicsburg beat us last week (at the district race). We ended up beating them by a decent amount (33 points). It's cool to see the pieces start to come together." MG junior Gwen Hershner led the pack with a 17th in 20:03. She was followed by freshman Hayden Combs (29th, 20:36), sophomore Leona Schwartz (42nd, 21:11), senior Sophie Mosher (44th, 21:11), freshman Paisley Douglas (74th, 22:18), freshman Callie Ziemba (103rd, 23:03) and freshman Jazmyne Floyd (159th, 25:32). That's six underclassmen in the top seven. "They're young," Hayes said. "It's getting them used to there's privilege with pressure. We train all this time and do all these things and we get to this moment and we're allowed to feel anxious and excited. It doesn't mean we have to change who we are. It's getting them to know the results are important but don't matter. "It's great to see that for them. They are a great group of girls, and they've been working hard." item.title: Why NASCAR's return to Homestead changes the championship challenge
item.description: He remembers watching his heroes race there. Even saw it in person a couple times as a kid. “It was just what I remember the championship being,” said Trackhouse Racing driver Ross Chastain , a native of Alva, Florida. For the first time since 2019, NASCAR’s season finale returns to Homestead-Miami Speedway this weekend. The sport ended every campaign there from 2002 through 2019 before spending the last six years in the desert at Phoenix Raceway . “There’s a lot of nostalgia for it, but there’s good reason for it,” Team Penske driver Austin Cindric said. Though Chastain and Cindric reside outside the small group of championship contenders, the Cup Series veterans know what Kyle Larson, Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin face Sunday. Homestead and Phoenix are viewed as two of the best tracks in the sport. But each offers different challenges. “Completely different racetracks,” Cindric said. How so? “We have a different aero package, a different engine package, different tires, different circuits and, really, different priorities,” he said. “Homestead, that highlight is not only the unique lines that you might have to run there to make speed, kind of running up by the wall, but also this tire fall-off and how it changes over the course of a run.” OK, so pretty much everything. Let’s start from the beginning. Homestead uses a taller spoiler than Phoenix, which creates more drag. Phoenix provides more horsepower. While Homestand remains the standard 670, NASCAR bumped the configuration to 750 horses at a handful of venues, including Phoenix, for 2026. At 1.5 miles and 18-20-degree banking in the corners, Homestead is the larger track. Drivers often stay inches from the wall in order to generate maximum speed off those higher turns. “You come off Turn 2 and Turn 4 and you’ve got a long straightaway to look at the next corner and think about what you could do better,” Chastain said. “Even if you’re just on a slight curve, you might be foot-on-the-floor wide open, but there’s a little bit of different nuances to driving straight than those slight curves at a track like Las Vegas.” At Phoenix, drivers usually hug the bottom. It’s a shorter route around the 1-mile circuit. Phoenix also features less banking (9-11 degrees) and an unusual dogleg on the frontstretch. But constants exist. No matter where the Cup Series goes, the drivers jostle with the best in the world. That’ll really be the case at 3 p.m. Sunday when Larson will clinch the title or Bell or Hamlin will spring a miraculous upset. “If you miss one small variable and you get that wrong, you’re not going to win,” Chastain said. “There’s just no way. You have to be buttoned up on so many things as drivers. I train with some other ones. We get granular on every little nuance of the racetrack. “It all comes down to where the rubber meets the road. The four tires hit the racetrack and nothing else matters than that once we get to Sunday.” This article originally appeared on The Daytona Beach News-Jo

Police confirm seizure of recreational weapons Authorities were quick to ease any major public safety concerns regarding the ordeal. A spokesperson for Northumbria Police confirmed that officers responded swiftly to the afternoon sighting. "Shortly after 1.55pm (Wednesday), we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area," the spokesperson stated. They went on to clarify that the situation was safely resolved and posed no broader danger to the community. "Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows," the statement continued. "At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing." Bizarre coincidence as team-mates pass by In a strange twist of fate during the roadside stop, two familiar faces happened to drive past the unfolding scene. The report added that Newcastle backup goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived by pure chance while officers were speaking with their colleague, pulling over to offer assistance. item.title: Florida State's search should start with Stein, Dillingham, Dickert
item.description: A sitting head coach with experience … but not too much experience. That should be Florida State’s plan of pursuit to replace Mike Norvell , who was mercifully fired on Nov. 1 and sent packing with memories of 2023 (13-1 record) and a $50 million buyout. The Seminoles, despite eight years of at least five losses in the last decade (!), are a big boy program playing in a talent-rich state. It is not the job for a first-time coach facing a significant rebuild. Experience in the hot seat should be a pre-requisite. But Seminoles fans should also want somebody who can be a long-term answer. Brian Kelly , 65, wants the job. Jimbo Fisher , 61, would take the job for the federal minimum wage. No thanks. The Seminoles’ search , once they hire an athletic director (which should be done first), should start with three names. I would call Kentucky’s Will Stein just to make sure he says no. If he’s interested in leaving the Wildcats after one year, every single resource should be devoted to pursuing him. Yes, he just has the single season as a big whistle, but he’s worth it. If Stein isn’t in play, my next two calls would be to Kenny Dillingham at Arizona State and Jake Dickert at Wake Forest. Dillingham, 36, is 26-21 for the Sun Devils and was an FSU assistant in 2020-21 and before that, was at Auburn for one year. Arizona State is 4-4 this year. Dickert, 43, has won at Washington State and Wake Forest. Think about that. He was 23-20 at Washington State and 14-5 at Wake (only loss this year is to Miami). A big leap from Winston-Salem to Tallahassee? Yes, but I want a guy who has turned programs around. That’s my list: 1. Stein; 2. Dillingham; 3. Dickert. item.description: Today in Boston Celtics history, Reggie Lewis made his debut for the team in a 125-108 victory against the Milwaukee Bucks in 1987. Born on this date in Baltimore, Maryland, Lewis played his college basketball at Northeastern University under renowned coach Jim Calhoun, who is better known for his tenure at UConn than his time in Massachusetts. Lewis was picked up by Boston with the 22nd overall pick of the 1987 NBA Draft. He later collapsed and died of heart-related medical issues that he'd been recently diagnosed with many years later but would play with Boston for six seasons, starting with this win over the Bucks. The Maryland native logged 4 points in 5 minutes of game time in his debut. Transactions In 1991 on this date, the Celtics signed Rickey Green as a free agent. The (at that time) 13-season veteran arrived in Boston for what proved the last stop of his NBA career and averaged 4.1 points and 2.6 assists per game over 26 tilts with the club. It is also the birthday of Steve Kuberski, born this day in Moline, Illinois. A product of Bradley, Kuberski would be drafted by the Celtics with the 59th pick of the 1969 NBA draft. He played eight seasons with Boston interrupted by single-season stints with the Milwaukee Bucks and Buffalo Braves (now Los Angeles Clippers ), winning titles with the team in 1974 and 1976. Historic milestones Other player debuts on this day include four other Celtics, beginning with Brad Lohaus, whose first game was playing alongside Lewis', scoring 8 points, 7 rebounds, and an assist. That game also saw Mark Acres play his inaugural game for the Celtics, scoring 4 points, 3 boards, and as many assists in nine minutes of playing time. This date also saw Matt Wenstrom take the floor for the first time with Boston in 1993. It came in a 100-88 victory over the Washington Bullets (now, Wizards), with Wenstrom going scoreless in just one minute of floor time. It is also the anniversary of Demetrius Jackson's debut for the team. The Notre Dame alum played for Boston for the first time in 2016 in a 123-107 loss to the Denver Nuggets, scoring 8 points, 3 boards, and 2 assists. Finally, it is also the date of the first game called by Celtics broadcasting legends Mike Gorman and Tommy Heinsohn (rest in peace) in 1981. It was a 111-94 win for Boston over the Indiana Pacers at the old Boston Garden that saw Celtics legend Larry Bird lead the team with 28 points and 14 rebounds.
